USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Mucolysis with an ineffective cough

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A man with neuromuscular weakness receives inhaled acetylcysteine for retained tenacious secretions. The secretions become thinner and more abundant, but his cough remains too weak to clear them. Coarse airway sounds persist. Which additional measure most directly addresses the problem?

  1. Restricting all respiratory physiotherapy
  2. Waiting for the secretions to be absorbed through bronchial mucosa
  3. Assisted airway clearance with suction when necessary
  4. Escalating mucolytic treatment without assessing clearance
  5. Suppressing the cough reflex with an opioid
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Assisted airway clearance with suction when necessary

Liquefying mucus does not remove it; an ineffective cough may require mechanical suction and other clearance support.

Understanding the options

Assisted airway clearance with suction when necessary
Suction can maintain an open airway when cough cannot clear liquefied secretions.
Escalating mucolytic treatment without assessing clearance
More liquid secretions may worsen retention if clearance is inadequate.
Suppressing the cough reflex with an opioid
Cough suppression can further impair removal.
Restricting all respiratory physiotherapy
Airway-clearance support remains important after mucolysis.
Waiting for the secretions to be absorbed through bronchial mucosa
Bronchial absorption is not a reliable substitute for clearing accumulated secretions.
